handoff.objective: Establish M -- the number of ciphertexts decapsulable under ONE encapsulation key -- across standardised and deployed ML-KEM uses. THIS TASK GATES THE ENTIRE CAMPAIGN, because G <= log2 M holds UNCONDITIONALLY by convexity: with f(beta) = -log2 p(beta) convex and the single-target optimiser at f'(beta_1) = -0.292, log2 M = f(beta_M) >= f(beta_1) + f'(beta_1)(beta_M - beta_1) = G. M is therefore the ceiling on the whole mechanism, and it is set by deployment specifications rather than by mathematics.

handoff.objective: Measure R = ||pi_{d-beta}(e)||^2 / ||e||^2 for CBD errors against real BKZ-reduced q-ary bases, and adjudicate whether its LEFT TAIL -- the part the best-of-M argument actually consumes -- obeys Beta(beta/2,(d-beta)/2).
handoff.why_the_ratio: DIVIDING BY ||e||^2 IS THE LOAD-BEARING DESIGN CHOICE. IDEA-3d71ca's A-vs-B decision rule was SCREENED OUT BEFORE THIS BATCH as forced: the ratio of the two competing relative variances is the identity kappa/2 exactly, for every d and every beta, verified numerically to 5.55e-15. Dividing by ||e||^2 cancels the norm fluctuation, hence cancels kappa, hence removes that identity. This statistic is the non-forced residual that survives the screen.
handoff.instrument: fpylll 0.6.4 + cysignals from the manylinux wheel into a task-local --target dir. No Sage, no g6k. Record wheel version and hashes in the receipt. A failed install is an INFRASTRUCTURE outcome under rule 5, never negative evidence.
handoff.cells: d in {100,140}, k = d/2, q = 3329, beta in {30,40}; 8 INDEPENDENT bases per cell (independent A, independent seeds), LLL then BKZ-beta with max_loops=2. 2^20 CBD_{eta=2} error vectors per basis -- ML-KEM's actual e/e1 law, not Gaussian.
headline_quantities: (a) KS distance of the empirical CDF of R to Beta(beta/2,(d-beta)/2) on the BODY -- a sanity check, NOT the finding
(b) empirical lower quantiles at 2^-10 and 2^-16 DIVIDED BY the Beta quantiles at the same levels -- this is the quantity the mechanism consumes
(c) between-basis versus within-basis variance decomposition of R over the 8 bases
forced_values_derived_in_advance: E[R] IS FORCED AND CARRIES ZERO INFORMATION. For any fixed rank-beta projector P and e with iid equal-variance coordinates, E||Pe||^2 = sigma^2 tr(P) = sigma^2 beta and E||e||^2 = sigma^2 d, so E[R] = beta/d to first order FOR EVERY BASIS, REDUCED OR NOT. Report it and never read it as agreement.

THE BETA LAW IS DERIVED, NOT FITTED. If pi behaves as a Haar-random beta-dim subspace with respect to e's direction, R ~ Beta(beta/2,(d-beta)/2) exactly for directionally-uniform e, and CBD coordinates are directionally uniform to O(d^-1/2) in the body. Its variance is 2 beta (d-beta) / (d^2 (d+2)). Quoted here so that 'measured variance approximately equals prediction' cannot be presented as a discovery.
THEREFORE THE ONLY NON-FORCED CONTENT IS (b) AND (c).

coordinator_defects_found_by_this_task.raised_by: TASK-20260805-708b70, self-reported as D1 and D2

D2_the_material_one.defect: THE SENSITIVITY DEMONSTRATION I DECLARED HAS EXPECTED CONTRAST EXACTLY ZERO. For a Haar-random rank-beta projector drawn INDEPENDENTLY of e, R = ||Pe||^2/||e||^2 is EXACTLY Beta(beta/2,(d-beta)/2) for every fixed e != 0, by rotation invariance. So the marginal law is Beta for ANY error law, including the two-block anisotropic error I specified as the demonstration arm. The gate could not fire.
D2_the_material_one.why_it_is_mine: The card required the demonstration's effect to be 'computable in closed form beforehand'. I computed it for E[R] -> tr(P Sigma)/tr(Sigma) and never checked it for the DECLARED STATISTIC, which is the mean over Haar draws of the 2^-10 quantile ratio. This is KN-TECH-1a5b7e MODE 1 applied to the sensitivity demonstration itself: I built the batch around a forced-quantity screen and put a forced quantity inside the screen's own control.
D2_the_material_one.executor_conduct_recorded_because_it_was: It ran the demonstration exactly as declared, reported the failure exactly as declared, and DID NOT SUBSTITUTE the statistic that works. It found one -- Var_P(E[R|P]) moves 1.26e-08 -> 1.51e-05, a factor 1198, against a closed form of 1.497e-05, agreeing to 0.69% -- reported it, labelled it as not the declared statistic, and left it UNUSED. Swapping a working control in post hoc would have rescued my broken design and produced a validation that meant nothing. It also proved the zero-contrast claim constructively: e = (1,0,...,0) over 16,384 Haar draws gives KS p = 0.572 against Beta(15,35).
D2_the_material_one.consequence: C3 is NOT met. Branch adjudicated NEITHER; outcome invalid_measurement -- explicitly not a negative observation and not an infrastructure error. Per this goal's non_terminal_conditions an instrument failure closes nothing.
D2_the_material_one.fix_for_the_next_batch: AN AMENDMENT, NOT A RERUN -- a rerun cannot repair a zero expected contrast. Either (a) couple the projector to the error law so the demonstration can move the declared statistic, or (b) declare the threshold on Var_P(E[R|P]), whose closed form is already verified to 0.69%. Whichever is chosen, the new demonstration's expected contrast must be DERIVED FOR THE DECLARED STATISTIC before the card is frozen.
